text: Square corners tore the world's first jet airliner open in the sky.
The de Havilland Comet had a pressurised cabin. On every flight, the air inside pushed the skin outward, then let it relax.
Around a round hole, that stress flows smoothly. But at a sharp corner, it piles up, several times higher.
Flight after flight, tiny cracks grew from the corners, until the skin split open.
That's why every airliner window you'll ever look through has rounded corners.
Three Comets broke up before anyone figured it out. Full video on my channel.
